Chromium is a chemical element; it has symbol Cr and atomic number 24.
In what year was Nikola Tesla born?
Nikola Tesla (10 July 1856 – 7 January 1943) was a Serbian-American engineer, futurist, and inventor.
In what year was Möbius strip discovered?
Möbius strip: In mathematics, a Möbius strip, Möbius band, or Möbius loop is a surface that can be formed by attaching the ends of a strip of paper together with a half-twist.
R (programming language): Robert Gentleman. R is a programming language for statistical computing and data visualization.
Prunus domestica: People's Republic of China. Prunus domestica is a species of flowering plant in the family Rosaceae.
Which country is McDonnell Douglas F-15E Strike Eagle from?

McDonnell Douglas F-15E Strike Eagle: United States. The McDonnell Douglas (now Boeing) F-15E Strike Eagle is an American all-weather multirole strike fighter derived from the McDonnell Douglas F-15 Eagle.
Who is credited with discovering Nihonium?
Nihonium: Joint Institute for Nuclear Research. Nihonium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Nh and atomic number 113.
Who is credited with discovering Mass–energy equivalence?
Mass–energy equivalence: Albert Einstein. In physics, mass–energy equivalence is the relationship between mass and energy in a system's rest frame.
Who is credited with discovering Plesiosaurus?
Plesiosaurus: Mary Anning. It is known by nearly complete skeletons from the Lias of England.
First nominated by Ronald Reagan in 1987 and reappointed every four years until 2006, this economist ran the Federal Reserve for its second-longest tenure ever — who is he?
Alan Greenspan (born March 6, 1926) is an American economist who served as the 13th chairman of the Federal Reserve from 1987 to 2006.
This English number theorist became a mathematical legend by proving Fermat's Last Theorem, earning the 2016 Abel Prize and a knighthood. Who is he?
Andrew Wiles (born 11 April 1953) is an English mathematician and a Royal Society Research Professor at the University of Oxford, specialising in number theory.

A German former computer repair technician, this man received international attention after murdering and cannibalizing a voluntary victim he had found over the Internet in March 2001, and was ultimately convicted of murder in a 2006 retrial — who is he?

Armin Meiwes (born 1 December 1961) is a German former computer repair technician who received international attention for murdering and cannibalising Bernd Brandes, whom he had found via the Internet as a voluntary victim, in March 2001.
The second-largest living rodents after capybaras, these large semiaquatic mammals of the Northern Hemisphere have webbed back feet, hand-like front paws, and flat, scaly tails — name the animal?
Beaver (genus Castor) are large semiaquatic rodents of the Northern Hemisphere.

Believed to descend from hounds kept at a Belgian abbey and used by police worldwide to track escaped prisoners, this scent hound can discern a person's trail days after they've passed — name this dog breed?
Bloodhound is a large scent hound, originally bred for hunting deer, wild boar, rabbits, and since the Middle Ages, for tracking people.
This condition results from inflamed, fluid-filled sacs that cushion friction points between bones, tendons, and muscles, commonly striking the shoulder, elbow, hip, or knee — what is it?
Bursitis is the inflammation of one or more bursae in the body.
This large, stocky black corvid fills a niche across Eurasia comparable to a similar bird found in North America, but is bigger and huskier than its transatlantic counterpart — what species is it?
Carrion crow (Corvus corone) is a passerine bird of the family Corvidae, native to western Europe and the eastern Palearctic.
Besides identifying the laws of elastic collision, this Dutch polymath studied Saturn's rings and improved the design of the telescope — who is he?
Christiaan Huygens (14 April 1629 - 8 July 1695) was a Dutch mathematician, physicist, engineer, astronomer, and inventor who is regarded as a key figure in the Scientific Revolution.
This activity involves designing algorithms and writing code in high-level languages so a machine can follow step-by-step instructions to perform tasks. What is it?
Computer programming is the composition of sequences of instructions, called programs, that computers can follow to perform tasks.
This Zambian-born economist turned four of her five books into New York Times bestsellers, including a provocative argument that foreign aid actually holds Africa back — who is she?
Dambisa Moyo, Baroness Moyo (born 2 February 1969) is a Zambian-born economist and author, known for her analysis of macroeconomics and global affairs.
Made from a fermented batter of ground black gram and rice, this thin South Indian bread is traditionally served with chutney and sambar — what is it?

Dosa (food) (in Indian English) or thosai (in Malaysian English and Singapore English) is a thin, savoury batter bread in South Indian cuisine made from a fermented batter of ground black gram and rice.

These ductless glands throughout the body secrete their products directly into the bloodstream rather than through a duct — together with the pineal, pituitary, thyroid, and others, what are they called?
Endocrine gland is a network of glands and organs located throughout the body.
This Chinese-born American computer scientist built ImageNet, the dataset that supercharged computer vision in the 2010s, and co-directs Stanford's Human-Centered AI institute — who is she?

Fei-Fei Li (pinyin: L Fifi; born July 3, 1976) is a Chinese-born American computer scientist best known for establishing ImageNet, the dataset that enabled rapid advances in computer vision in the 2010s.

Found from the tropics to subarctic regions and accounting for about 88% of living amphibian species, this tailless, semiaquatic creature has a name that informally splits into 'toad' for the warty ones — what is it?
Frog is any member of a diverse and largely semiaquatic group of short-bodied, tailless amphibian vertebrates composing the order Anura (coming from the Ancient Greek, literally 'without tail').
One of the most widely distributed eagles in the Northern Hemisphere, this raptor is dark brown with lighter plumage on its nape and white markings on immature birds — which bird of prey?
Golden eagle (Aquila chrysaetos) is a bird of prey living in the Northern Hemisphere.

This now-outdated astronomical model placed the Sun rather than the Earth at the center of the universe, eventually replacing the geocentric view before itself being superseded by relativity — what model is it?
Heliocentrism (also known as the heliocentric model) is a superseded astronomical model that placed the Sun at the center of the universe, with the Earth and the planets in its orbit.

Also called prussic acid, this highly toxic and flammable liquid boils just above room temperature at 25.6 degrees Celsius. It is produced industrially as a precursor to many chemical compounds, particularly potassium cyanide and adiponitrile. What is it?
Hydrogen cyanide (also called prussic acid) is a chemical compound with the formula HCN and structural formula HCN.
Founder of Romania's Social Democratic Party, this engineer served two separate stints as president after playing a leading role in the 1989 revolution that toppled Ceaușescu — who is he?

Ion Iliescu (3 March 1930 - 5 August 2025) was a Romanian politician and engineer who served as the first and third President of Romania since the country's transition to democracy, from 1990 to 1996 and 2000 to 2004.
Originally trained as a mathematician, this English economist built the foundation for an entire school of macroeconomic thought that bears his name — who is he?

John Maynard Keynes (KAYNZ; 5 June 1883 - 21 April 1946), was an English economist whose writings are considered the basis for the school of thought known as Keynesian economics, as well as its various offshoots.
When the natural curve of the thoracic spine exceeds about 45 degrees, doctors give this excessive rounding of the upper back a name rooted in the Greek word for 'hump' — what is it?
Kyphosis (from Greek (kyphos) 'hump') is an abnormally excessive convex curvature of the spine as it occurs in the thoracic and sacral regions.
Serving as a somatosensory organ as well as a tool for eating and forming sounds, this pair of soft facial features is one of the most visible parts of the mouth — what are they?
Lip are a horizontal pair of soft appendages attached to the jaws and are the most visible part of the mouth of many animals, including humans.
Roughly 60% the diameter of Pluto and stained reddish-brown by tholins, this trans-Neptunian dwarf planet carries minor-planet number 136472 — what is it?
Makemake (minor-planet number 136472) is a dwarf planet orbiting the Sun in the Kuiper belt, a disc of icy bodies beyond the orbit of Neptune.
This genus of about 20 species in the Lamiaceae family readily hybridizes where different species' ranges overlap, and thrives best in wet, moist soils — what genus is it?
Mentha (from Greek mntha, Linear B mi-ta), is a genus of flowering plants in the mint family, Lamiaceae.

Native to Africa, Asia, and Oceania, with one invasive species now in the southern U.S., this reptile genus ranges from 20 centimeters long to over 3 meters in the Komodo dragon — name this group of lizards?
Monitor lizard are lizards in the genus Varanus, the only extant genus in the family Varanidae.

Discovered in 1898 alongside krypton and xenon, this colorless noble gas is famous for the distinctive bright-red glow it emits, which led to its immediate identification as a new element — what gas, symbol Ne, is it?
Neon is a chemical element; it has the symbol Ne and the atomic number 10.

This branch of medicine focuses on the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of cancer, a disease first documented in Egypt as early as 3000 BCE in the Edwin Smith papyrus — what is this medical specialty called?
Oncology is a branch of medicine that deals with the study, treatment, diagnosis, and prevention of cancer.
Named after a 17th-century French mathematician and physicist, this SI unit of pressure is defined as one newton of force per square metre — name the unit?
Pascal (unit) (symbol: Pa) is the unit of pressure in the International System of Units (SI).
Ranging in color from clear to yellow, green, or even grey, this respiratory mucus is expelled through coughing and also goes by the name sputum — what is it?
Phlegm (Ancient) is mucus produced by the respiratory system, excluding that produced by the throat and nose passages.
Ranging from linear chains to heavily branched polymers, these carbohydrate compounds — like starch, glycogen, and chitin — consist of many simple sugar units linked together. What are they called?
Polysaccharide (from Ancient Greek (pols) 'many, much' and (skkhar) 'sugar') are "compounds consisting of a large number of monosaccharides linked glycosidically".
Nesting in burrows or rock crevices on coastal cliffs, this black-and-white seabird can dive underwater to feed and beats its short wings up to 400 times per minute in flight — what bird is it?
Puffin are any of three species of small alcids (auks) in the bird genus Fratercula.
Which large Southern African dog breed, whose standard was drafted in 1922 in what's now Zimbabwe, descends from ridged hunting dogs of the Khoikhoi crossed with European breeds used to bay lions?
Rhodesian Ridgeback is a large dog breed originally bred in Southern Africa.
Once placed in its own plant family before molecular studies folded it into Dracaena, this African and Asian succulent genus includes the plant nicknamed 'devil's tongue' — which genus?

Sansevieria is a historically recognized genus of flowering plants, native to Africa, notably Madagascar, and southern Asia, now included in the genus Dracaena on the basis of molecular phylogenetic studies.
Named for its enormous shoe-shaped bill, this grey wading bird of East African swamps was once filed with storks but now sits beside pelicans — and its closest kin is the hamerkop — what is it?
Shoebill (Balaeniceps rex), also known as the whale-headed stork, whalebill, and shoe-billed stork, is a large long-legged wading bird.

This class of moisture-loving hexapods — the largest lineage of six-legged creatures excluded from the insect group — indirectly aids decomposition by breaking down organic matter and shaping soil microbial life. What are they?
Springtail (class Collembola) form the largest of the three lineages of modern hexapods that are no longer considered insects, the others being Protura and Diplura.
Serving as prime minister seven separate times before becoming president from 1993 to 2000, this Turkish statesman led two different political parties across his long career — who was he?
Süleyman Demirel (1 November 1924 - 17 June 2015) was a Turkish politician, engineer, and statesman who served as the president of Turkey from 1993 to 2000.
This herb is also called common thyme or garden thyme and belongs to the mint family, Lamiaceae — which species is it?
Thymus vulgaris (common thyme, German thyme, garden thyme or just thyme) is a species of flowering plant in the mint family, Lamiaceae.
This break in the skin or mucous membrane involves tissue breakdown severe enough to expose the dermis or fat beneath, and often becomes infected with pus — what condition is it?
Ulcer (dermatology) is a sore on the skin or a mucous membrane, accompanied by the disintegration of tissue.
This unit of time, equal to seven days, serves as the standard calendrical period between a day and a month in most of the world. What is it?
Week (in the Western and international context) is a unit of time equal to seven days.
Also known as the empirical guideline, this statistical shorthand describes the percentage of values within one, two, and three standard deviations of the mean in a normal distribution — which one?
Transmitted by the bite of an infected tsetse fly, this parasitic infection caused by Trypanosoma brucei is better known in humans as 'sleeping sickness' — what's its formal name?
African trypanosomiasis: Parasitic disease also known as sleeping sickness.
With more than 1,100 species including onions, garlic, leeks, and chives, this is the largest genus in the flowering plant family Amaryllidaceae — which genus?
Allium: Genus of flowering plants. The flowers form an umbel at the top of a leafless stalk.
This Russian physicist miraculously survived a 1978 accident in which a high-energy proton beam from a particle accelerator passed directly through his skull — who is he?
Anatoli Bugorski: Soviet and Russian scientist (born 1942)
Known by common names like greenfly and blackfly, these small sap-sucking insects reproduce via live-born nymphs without males, a trick called telescoping generations — what are they?
Aphid: Superfamily of insects. The group includes the fluffy white woolly aphids.
Originally conceived as the average Earth-Sun distance before its 2012 redefinition, this measure equals about 499 light-seconds and underpins the definition of the parsec — what is it called?
Astronomical unit: Mean distance between Earth and the Sun.
Sitting at the bottom of the forebrain and including the striatum and substantia nigra, this cluster of brain nuclei governs voluntary movement and habit formation — what is it called?
Basal ganglia: Group of subcortical nuclei involved in the motor and reward systems.
Also known as vitamin B7, this B vitamin is found in every living cell and is popularly sold as a supplement; isolated, it's a white needle-like crystal — what is it?
Biotin: Chemical compound and essential nutrient.
This rigid organ not only supports the body and enables movement but also manufactures both red and white blood cells and stores essential minerals — what is it?
Bone: Rigid organs of the skeleton of vertebrates.

Marketed as Wellbutrin, this atypical antidepressant doubles as a stop-smoking aid and stands out for not causing sexual dysfunction or weight gain — what is this norepinephrine-dopamine reuptake inhibitor?
Bupropion: Medication mainly used for depression and smoking cessation.
This golden fungus — also known as 'girolle' — is often confused with a poisonous lookalike, though it remains a prized edible mushroom and the type species of its genus — which one is it?
Cantharellus cibarius: Species of fungus. Despite its characteristic features, C. cibarius can be confused with species such as the poisonous Omphalotus illudens.
Marketed as Zinacef and used against everything from meningitis to Lyme disease, this second-generation cephalosporin antibiotic was patented in 1971 — which drug?
Cefuroxime: Antibiotic medication. It is used by mouth or by injection into a vein or muscle.
Nicknamed the sea wasp, this Australian box jellyfish is considered the world's most lethal, with venom-laced tentacles up to 10 feet long — which species?
Chironex fleckeri: Species of jellyfish. It has been described as "the most lethal jellyfish in the world", with at least 64 known deaths in Australia from 1884 to 2021.
This little Indo-Pacific reef fish, banded in white, shelters among stinging tentacles and repays the favor by fending off anemone-eaters and fanning its host clean. What fish is it?
Named after a Quechua word meaning the same thing, this New World vulture — with Andean and Californian species — is the largest flying land bird in the Western Hemisphere. What is it?
Condor: Name for two species of vultures.
Commonly called comb jellies, these are the largest animals that swim using rows of cilia, drifting through every ocean as masses of two-layered jelly — what's the phylum?
Ctenophora: Phylum of gelatinous marine animals.
This biological process, powered by rhythmic muscle waves called peristalsis, expels solid waste from the digestive tract through the anus or cloaca — what is it?
Defecation: Expulsion of feces from the digestive tract.
A dentist and gambler who fought alongside lawman Wyatt Earp at the O.K. Corral, his reputation claimed dozens of killings though researchers count just one to three — who was this gunfighter?
Doc Holliday: Gambler, gunfighter, and dentist in the American West (1851–1887)
After stints at the CIA, Dell, and Booz Allen Hamilton, this NSA contractor flew to Hong Kong in 2013 and leaked thousands of classified documents exposing global surveillance — who is he?
Edward Snowden: Whistleblower and NSA contractor (born 1983)
One of the four basic animal tissue types, this thin protective cell layer lines blood vessels and body cavities and includes the skin's outer layer — what is it called?
Epithelium: Tissue lining the surfaces of organs in animals.
In this small bird of prey, females can be up to 25% larger than males — one of the biggest size gaps between sexes of any bird — and it hunts garden songbirds across Europe and Asia — which raptor?

Eurasian sparrowhawk: Species of bird. The Eurasian sparrowhawk (Accipiter nisus), also known as the northern sparrowhawk or simply the sparrowhawk, is a small bird of prey in the family Accipitridae.
Marketed under brand names like Allegra, this second-generation antihistamine treats allergy symptoms without crossing the blood-brain barrier the way older drugs do — what medication is it?
Fexofenadine: Antihistamine medication. Fexofenadine is an antihistamine medication used in the treatment of allergy symptoms such as allergic rhinitis and urticaria.
Dead at just 26, this British thinker had already reshaped philosophy, mathematics and economics — and as an undergraduate translated Wittgenstein's 'Tractatus' into English; who was he?
Frank P. Ramsey: British philosopher, mathematician and economist (1903–1930)
With a siphon that can stretch over three feet and a shell just 6 to 8 inches across, this giant Pacific burrowing clam can live up to 179 years — which creature?
Caused by the bacterium Neisseria gonorrhoeae and colloquially called 'the clap,' this sexually transmitted infection can pass from mother to child during birth — what is it?
Gonorrhea: Sexually transmitted infection. Gonorrhea or gonorrhoea, colloquially known as the clap, is a sexually transmitted infection (STI) caused by the bacterium Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
This standard markup language structures web documents using elements delineated by tags, often paired with CSS and JavaScript — what is it?
HTML: Markup language for documents. Hypertext Markup Language (HTML) is the standard markup language for documents designed to be displayed in a web browser.
This inflammation of the liver can cause jaundice and, if it becomes chronic, progress to cirrhosis — most commonly caused by five different viruses labeled A through E. What condition is it?
Hepatitis: Inflammation of the liver. Hepatitis is acute if it resolves within six months, and chronic if it lasts longer than six months.
The most widespread of all primates, this bipedal, nearly hairless species owes its advanced technology, culture, and language to a large, complex brain — what is it?
Human: Species of hominid in the genus Homo.

This crystalline mineral form of frozen water occurs naturally on Earth, other planets, and even in Oort cloud objects, and has at least nineteen known phases depending on temperature and pressure — what is it?
Ice: Frozen water; the solid state of water.
This purplish-black Brazilian fruit doesn't dangle from branches — it sprouts straight out of the tree trunk itself. What is it?
Jabuticaba: Tree in the family Myrtaceae.
This English scientist's 1808 book, 'A New System of Chemical Philosophy,' laid the foundations of modern atomic theory, and he also kept daily weather records for over fifty years — who was he?
John Dalton: British chemist and physicist (1766–1844)
Convicted in 1995 of fraud and illegally intercepting communications, this hacker served five years in prison before founding his own computer-security consulting firm — who is he?

The smallest member of the genus Mustela, this slender carnivore has been introduced to New Zealand, Malta, Crete, the Azores, and São Tomé despite being native across Eurasia and North Africa — what is it?
Defined as exactly one cubic decimetre and rooted in an old French unit called the litron, what metric measure of volume is this?
Litre: Unit of volume. The litre (Commonwealth spelling) or liter (American spelling) (SI symbols L and l, other symbol used: ℓ) is a metric unit of volume.
Nicknamed the 'maker of modern Mysore,' this Indian civil engineer and statesman's birthday is now celebrated as Engineer's Day across India, Sri Lanka, and Tanzania — who is he?
M. Visvesvaraya: Indian civil engineer, administrator, and former prime minister of Mysore Kingdom.

Studying under Rutherford at the Cavendish Lab, this Adelaide-born physicist discovered the nuclei of helium-3 and tritium and helped achieve the first experimental nuclear fusion — who was this Australian humanitarian?
This rose-family shrub, commonly known as the medlar, produces fruit that's traditionally eaten only after it has softened past ripeness — what's its scientific name?
Mespilus germanica: Fruit tree, the medlar. Mespilus germanica, known as the medlar or common medlar, is a large shrub or small tree in the rose family Rosaceae.
Awarded the 1976 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences, this University of Chicago economist championed monetarism over Keynesianism and mentored future laureates like Gary Becker — who is he?
Milton Friedman: American economist and statistician (1912–2006)
Produced by glands throughout the body's linings — including the respiratory, digestive, and urogenital tracts — which slippery substance traps and destroys harmful bacteria and viruses?
Mucus: Secretion produced by mucous membranes.

The Navy paid his Purdue aeronautical-engineering tuition under the Holloway Plan, and he flew the Grumman F9F Panther off the USS Essex in the Korean War before his most famous flight of all — which Ohio-born aviator was he?
Named for the daring Doolittle airmen of World War II, this subsonic stealth flying wing is being built to replace the B-1 and B-2 by 2040 — which aircraft is it?
Northrop Grumman B-21 Raider: American stealth bomber aircraft.

Traditionally eaten whole in French cuisine, with diners often covering their heads with a napkin while doing so, this small Eurasian songbird's population crashed from overhunting despite EU protection — which bird?
Ortolan bunting: Species of bird in Eurasia.
Defined as the distance at which one astronomical unit subtends an angle of one arcsecond, this unit equals about 3.26 light-years — which unit?
Parsec: Unit of length in astronomy.
Smaller than 3 millimetres and caused by leaking capillaries, these tiny red or purple skin spots can be forensically significant when found around the eyes or neck — what are they called?
Petechia: Small red or purple blemish on the skin, eyes, etc. due to rupture of capillaries.
Known as the Scots pine in Britain, this Eurasian conifer is identifiable by its blue-green needles and orange-red bark — which species?
Pinus sylvestris: Species of conifer. Pinus sylvestris is a species of tree in the pine family Pinaceae that is native to Eurasia.
Also known as niter or saltpeter, this compound is a key ingredient of traditional gunpowder and gives cured meats their reddish color — what is it?
Potassium nitrate: Chemical compound. Potassium nitrate is a chemical compound with a sharp, salty, bitter taste and the chemical formula KNO3.
The earliest vertebrates known to achieve powered flight, these warm-blooded Mesozoic reptiles had wings stretched from ankle to a dramatically lengthened fourth finger — what were they called?
Pterosaur: Extinct order of flying reptiles.

A pioneer in optical character recognition and speech synthesis, this futurist inventor received the National Medal of Technology from President Clinton in 1999 for his outlook on AI and life extension — who is he?
Ray Kurzweil: American computer scientist, author and futurist (born 1948)
Often called the first modern chemist, which 17th-century Anglo-Irish natural philosopher described the inverse relationship between a gas's pressure and volume in a law that bears his name?
Held together by electrostatic forces called ionic bonds, this type of chemical compound pairs positive and negative ions into a substance with zero net charge — what class of compound?
Salt (chemistry): Chemical compound involving ionic bonding.
A peptide mimicking a gut hormone, this drug treats type 2 diabetes as Ozempic and Rybelsus but is sold as Wegovy for weight loss — what's the underlying medication?
This altered state cycles between REM and non-REM modes, and despite outward stillness it still produces active brain patterns — more reactive than a coma. What is it?
Sleep: Naturally recurring resting state of mind and body.
Lacking any nervous, digestive, or circulatory system, these ancient sea-bound filter feeders pump water through pore-riddled bodies using flagella to survive — what are they?
Sponge: Animals of the phylum Porifera.
Nicknamed the "Super Flanker" and derived from the Su-27, this twin-engine, supermaneuverable Russian air superiority fighter first flew as a prototype in 1988 — what is it?
Sukhoi Su-35: Upgraded series of the Su-27 fighter aircraft.

A major constituent of bile and widely distributed in mammalian tissues, this compound is usually called an amino acid even though its sulfonic acid group keeps it out of protein synthesis. What is it?
Taurine: Aminosulfonic acid. Taurine is a major constituent of bile and can be found in the large intestine.
Nicknamed thunderflies, these minute fringe-winged insects are too feeble for normal flight, so they fly using a 'clap and fling' trick that conjures lift from tiny vortices. What are they?
Thrips: Order of insects. Thrips are a functionally diverse group; many of the known species are fungivorous.

This anabolic steroid, derived from the nandrolone group, is used legally in livestock to boost muscle growth but also circulates illegally on the black market under a shortened nickname — what is it?
Trenbolone: Anabolic steroid. Trenbolone is an androgen and anabolic steroid (AAS) of the nandrolone group which itself was never marketed for human use.
This medical specialty treats the kidneys, bladder and urinary tract, along with the male reproductive organs, covering conditions from infections to kidney stones — which field of medicine?
Urology: Medical specialty on the urinary and reproductive systems. The urinary and reproductive tracts are closely linked, and disorders of one often affect the other.
Sporting prominent tusks and whiskers, this Arctic pinniped's Pacific males can weigh over 2,000 kilograms, making it second in size among pinnipeds only to the elephant seals — what animal?
Walrus: Species of marine mammal with tusks.
Named for the Aztec god of fire and lightning, this ancient Mexican dog breed comes in hairless and fully-coated varieties within the same litter — which breed?
Xoloitzcuintle: Hairless dog breed from Mexico.
What is the chemical symbol for thallium?
The symbol for thallium is Tl. Thallium is a chemical element; it has symbol Tl and atomic number 81.
The symbol for osmium is Os. Osmium is a chemical element; it has symbol Os and atomic number 76.

Bob Hope is a comedian. Hope hosted the Academy Awards ceremony a record 19 times.
In what year was Cher born?
Cher (SHAIR; legally mononymous; born Cheryl Sarkisian, May 20, 1946) is an American singer and actress.
In what year was Olga Kurylenko born?
Olga Kurylenko: Olga Kostyantynivna Kurylenko (born 14 November 1979) is a Ukrainian-born French actress and former model.
In what year was Gal Gadot born?
Gal Gadot (Hebrew: גל גדות, pronounced [ˈɡal ɡaˈdot]; born 30 April 1985) is an Israeli actress.
In what year was Lily-Rose Depp born?
Lily-Rose Depp: Lily-Rose Melody Depp (born May 27, 1999) is a French and American actress and singer.
In what year was Fran Drescher born?
Fran Drescher: Francine Joy Drescher (born September 30, 1957) is an American actress, writer, comedian, producer, and former trade union leader.
In what year was Chuck Norris born?
Chuck Norris: Carlos Ray "Chuck" Norris (March 10, 1940 – March 19, 2026) was an American martial artist, actor, screenwriter, and author.
In what year was Prabhas born?
Prabhas made his acting debut with the drama Eeswar (2002) and later attained his breakthrough with the action romance Varsham (2004).
In what year was George Lucas born?
George Lucas: George Walton Lucas Jr. (born May 14, 1944) is an American filmmaker and philanthropist.
In what year was Golshifteh Farahani born?
Golshifteh Farahani: Rahavard Farahani (Persian: رهاورد فراهانی; born 10 July 1983), known professionally as Golshifteh Farahani (گلشیفته فراهانی), is an Iranian actress.
In what year was Robert Redford born?
Robert Redford: Redford began his career on television in the late 1950s, appearing in anthology series such as Alfred Hitchcock Presents and The Twilight Zone.
In what year was James Caan born?
James Caan: James Edmund Caan ( KAHN; March 26, 1940 – July 6, 2022) was an American actor.
In what year did Roald Dahl die?
Roald Dahl: Dahl was born in Wales to affluent Norwegian immigrant parents, and lived for most of his life in England.
